finding.claim: Stored client_secret is sent via HTTP Basic auth to a token endpoint of an authorization server chosen by the MCP server's 401 response, with no user interaction (client_credentials path). Confidence: medium-high; requires an untrusted or compromised MCP server and an oauth provider holding a client secret.
finding.source: WWW-Authenticate resource_metadata parameter in a 401 response from the MCP server (lib/mcp/client/http.rb:416), which is attacker-controlled
finding.sink: Basic Authorization header and form POST to token_endpoint carrying client_id and client_secret (lib/mcp/client/oauth/flow.rb:696, :707)

finding.guards_checked: HTTPS-only URLs (flow.rb:380-385, discovery.rb:181-194); issuer equality (flow.rb:402-412); PRM resource coverage (flow.rb:513-525); MCP URL must be HTTPS or loopback when oauth is set (http.rb:60). None binds stored credentials to the issuing AS; no issuer is persisted (in_memory_storage.rb:33-34). Variant: flow.rb:414-416 reuses stored client_information in the authorization_code path, sending the secret at flow.rb:658 after user consent at the attacker AS.

finding.claim: Stored refresh_token and client_secret are POSTed to a token endpoint of an authorization server selected by an untrusted 401 response, and the attacker's tokens are saved. No user interaction. Confidence: medium; requires a stored refresh token and an untrusted MCP server.
finding.source: WWW-Authenticate resource_metadata in a 401 response from the MCP server (lib/mcp/client/http.rb:416), combined with the stored refresh_token (flow.rb:138)
finding.sink: Refresh-token grant POST carrying refresh_token and Basic client secret to the attacker token_endpoint (flow.rb:178-183, 661-669, 696, 707)

finding.guards_checked: Stored client_information must exist (flow.rb:149-151); HTTPS on resource_metadata (flow.rb:153-155); PRM resource coverage and issuer equality (same as finding 1). Nothing records or compares the issuer of the stored refresh token (in_memory_storage.rb:33-34 stores a bare hash).

finding.claim: The client fetches attacker-named HTTPS URLs from the MCP server's 401 response and PRM, with no host or IP restriction. Error messages may reflect a fragment of the response body or connection error details, giving a limited reachability and content oracle on the user's network. Confidence: medium; low severity because the target must serve HTTPS with a trusted certificate.
finding.source: WWW-Authenticate resource_metadata (lib/mcp/client/http.rb:416) and PRM authorization_servers[0] (flow.rb:320-326), both attacker-controlled
finding.sink: http_get for PRM (flow.rb:208-214) and AS metadata (flow.rb:297-299) via fetch_metadata_json (flow.rb:333-367); parse and Faraday errors surfaced at flow.rb:340-348 and 336-341
